page.intro: The way most people whiten: slowly, at home, with trays made for your teeth.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: We take scans of your teeth and make thin trays that fit only you. You wear them with a small amount of gel for an hour or so each evening, for around three weeks.

sections.heading: What to expect
sections.text: Teeth lighten gradually. Some people feel sensitive for a day or two; if you do, you skip an evening or two and we give you something for it.

sections.heading: Afterwards
sections.text: Keep your trays. A tube of gel now and then keeps your teeth where you like them.

items.name: Whitening in the studio
items.line: One long visit here, then trays to finish at home.

page.intro: A head start in the chair, finished at home.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: Dr Marlie protects your gums and applies a stronger gel in the studio, in short rounds over about two hours. You take trays home to finish.

sections.heading: Who it suits
sections.text: People who want to see a change sooner, for an event or just because. It costs more than whitening at home and ends in the same place.

items.name: Composite bonding
items.line: Chips, small gaps and uneven edges built up in tooth-coloured resin.

page.intro: Small changes to shape, added rather than drilled away.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text: Dr Marlie adds resin, shaped and polished by hand, to the tooth's surface. Most people need nothing taken away from the tooth.

sections.heading: Looking after it
sections.text: Bonding can chip or stain like a tooth. We polish it at your hygiene visits and repair it if it chips.

items.name: Hygiene
items.line: A clean before any whitening, and every six months after.

page.intro: Whitening works best on clean teeth.

sections.heading: What happens
sections.text: Leah cleans above and below the gum line and polishes away surface stains, then shows you anything worth changing in how you brush.

whiteningPage.title: Whitening
whiteningPage.intro: By a dentist, at home or here.

ways.heading: At home
ways.text: Trays made for your teeth and a gentle gel, worn in the evenings for around three weeks. Most people start here.

ways.heading: In the studio
ways.text: About two hours in the chair with a stronger gel, then trays to finish at home. Sooner, and dearer.

ways.heading: How white
ways.text: We won't promise a shade. Teeth lighten from their own starting colour, and at consultation I'll show you what's realistic for yours.

whiteningPage.sensitivity: Some people feel sensitive for a day or two. If you do, skip an evening or two; we'll give you a toothpaste for it and slow the plan down.
whiteningPage.crowns: Crowns, veneers and fillings don't change colour. If you have them at the front, we plan around them before we start.

sections.heading: The first two days
sections.text: Go easy on coffee, red wine and anything that would stain a white shirt. Brush gently with the toothpaste we gave you.

sections.heading: Sensitivity
sections.text: A little is common and passes. If it doesn't after two days, stop wearing your trays and message us.

sections.heading: Bonding
sections.text: Treat it like your own teeth: no opening packets with them, and a night guard if we've given you one.

items.title: What whitening can and can't do
items.intro: It lightens your own teeth. It doesn't change crowns or fillings, and it fades slowly over time.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.text: Whitening gel lightens the colour inside the tooth. How far depends on where your teeth start, which is why I won't promise a shade before I've seen them.

sections.heading: What it doesn't
sections.text: Crowns, veneers and fillings stay the colour they are. If you have them at the front, we talk about that first.

sections.heading: Why a dentist
sections.text: In the UK, only a registered dentist, or a hygienist or therapist on a dentist's prescription, may whiten teeth. Kits sold elsewhere are weaker, or not legal.

items.title: Keeping your teeth white
items.intro: Whitening fades slowly. A few habits slow it further.

sections.heading: Day to day
sections.text: Rinse with water after coffee or red wine. Use a straw for iced coffee if you like.

sections.heading: Top-ups
sections.text: Keep your trays. A night or two with fresh gel once or twice a year is usually enough.

questions.q: Is whitening done by a dentist?
questions.a: Yes. Only a registered dentist, or a hygienist on a dentist's prescription, may whiten teeth in the UK. Dr Marlie prescribes every whitening here.

questions.q: How white will my teeth go?
questions.a: We won't promise a shade. At your consultation Dr Marlie shows you what's realistic for your teeth.

questions.q: Can I whiten if I'm under 18?
questions.a: No. We don't whiten teeth for anyone under 18.

questions.q: Will my crowns or fillings change colour?
questions.a: No. We plan around them before we start.

questions.q: Do I need a consultation first?
questions.a: Yes, always. It's 45 minutes and £45, taken off any treatment.
